(Spoiler alert, making some assumptions here as never worked on this code directly) 
I think it is a more complex bug here.
Admission plugin is relaying on NewCloud to return the right object, where the configuration is passed into NewCloud to be initialized with.
NewCloud is using az.InitializeCloudFromConfig(config, false). This implies secret is not used and merge never happens. 

On the other hand cloud controller, when starting is doing `Initialize()`, which calls `az.InitializeCloudFromSecret()` and merges configuration. This is good reason, as in admission plugin case, if ManagedIdentity is not used, we always end up with credentials in the file.
 
I suspect this was done to preserve backwards compatibility at some point.
Because calling `InitializeCloudFromSecret()` instead of `InitializeCloudFromConfig` would require `Config.CloudConfigType: file` in the cloud-config file. Otherwise, we need to pass fully merged config. So NewCloud behaviour was not touched. 

So this patch basically just prevents panic, but will not solve the main problem, that apiserver is initialized different way than cloud provider code. 

API server admission plugin code base is built around 2 cases - use managed Identity, or use the file with credentials. And 3rd case, where ConfigFile is non-sensitive data and secret is sensitive is dropped on the floor.

@mjudeikis the `InitializeCloudFromConfig`(or `InitializeCloudFromSecret`) actually succeeded, while there is no credentials in the config, this would lead to nil disksClient, and api-server would invoke `cloud.GettLabelsForVolume` and cause panic.
Is there a way to validate this PR in OpenShift env directly?

@andyzhangx I agree with @mjudeikis - this might prevent the panic, however depending on the cloud provider configuration in the API server, the labels might or might not be enriched.  That doesn't seem great.  Is there a way to ensure that DisksClient can be initialized from the Secret so that the labels are always enriched?

issue_context.title: GetLabelsForVolume panic issue for azure disk PV
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
Overview
========

A persistent volume claim / storage class configured in a certain way can cause all the Kube API servers on an ARO cluster to crashloop.

We’ve seen this issue on a production cluster (ICM 192488792).  In development we have proven one vector by which the cluster could have got into this state but it doesn’t seem that likely.  We wonder if there are other vectors.

We don’t currently have a good way to rescue a cluster that gets into this state because our service accesses are predicated on API server availability.

Request
=======

We would like help:

1. to agree and expedite an appropriate fix in order to protect all other production clusters.
2. with suggestions on how we might fix the broken production cluster.

Causes
======

1. In certain cases upon PV create, the persistentvolume admission controller attempts to retrieve the managed disk object via the Azure API, but in ARO the relevant client object is a nil pointer.  The pointer is dereferenced and the kube API server panics.

2. The PVC controller repeatedly attempts to create the PV object, which DoSes the kube API server.

3. The client object in (1) is nil because of ARO’s cloud provider authentication architecture, which differs from that of OCP.  More information below.

Technical detail
================

For a panic stack trace and reproducer, see

* Creation of an Azure Disk persistent volume is attempted
* The persistentvolume admission controller runs, (l
*persistentVolumeLabel) Admit(), in
vendor/k8s.io/kubernetes/plugin/pkg/admission/storage/persistentvolume/label/admission.go:104
* In our possible reproducer, the admission controller does not return early in (l *persistentVolumeLabel) findVolumeLabels(), admission.go:182 because the zone labels are not set.
* A cloud provider is (incorrectly) instantiated via:
   - getAzurePVLabeler(), admission.go:354
   - cloudprovider.GetCloudProvider(), admission.go:333
   - NewCloud(),
vendor/k8s.io/kubernetes/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/azure/azure.go:262
   - (az *Cloud) InitializeCloudFromConfig, azure.go:283
* We see the following loglines:
   - Azure cloud provider is starting without credentials
   - Azure cloudprovider using try backoff: retries=%d, exponent=%f, duration=%d, jitter=%f
* We believe that an early return occurs at azure.go:444, before c.DisksClient is initialised, because servicePrincipalToken is nil
* Later, a nil pointer dereference of c.DisksClient occurs in (c *Cloud) GetAzureDiskLabels,
vendor/k8s.io/kubernetes/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/azure/azure_managedDiskController.go:301

OCP 4.3 cloud provider authentication architecture ==================================================

* The installer lays down an Azure managed identity (MSI) resource, grants it Contributor access to cluster resource group and to any pre-existing virtual network (VNET).
* In the context of the Kube API server, the persistentvolume admission controller uses MSI to authenticate to Azure for its API calls.

ARO 4.3 cloud provider authentication architecture ==================================================

* ARO can’t follow OCP 4.3’s architecture because of the following chicken-and-egg problem:
   - As an Azure service, ARO is not permitted to add role assignments to the customer’s pre-existing virtual network - the customer must explicitly do this.
   - No cluster managed identity can exist before the customer runs `az aro create` (by definition), so there is nothing for the customer to grant the role assignment to.
* As a result, ARO does not use a managed identity at all, and instead uses a user-created cluster service principal.
* ARO carries a patch to the installer which creates a kube-config/azure-cloud-provider Secret during cluster install.  The controller manager merges the cloud config with this Secret at start-up time (see `InitializeCloudFromSecret()`), however this code path does not run in the API server.  In ARO, any calls to the Azure API from the API server are probably broken.
* Prior to GA, ARO wrote the cloud config secret raw into the cloud config.  Reverting to this behaviour would work around this issue, but is clearly suboptimal.
